elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Revised 22.1: "Vendor may audit Customer no more than once in any 12-month period".

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Revised 22.1: "on 30 days' written notice"; the prior "at any time without notice" language is deleted.

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: Revised 22.1: "by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality".

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: Revised 22.1: auditor is "bound by confidentiality"; reinforced by 22.3 treating findings as Customer Confidential Information.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Retained 22.2: "Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period" — already at the preferred 5% threshold, no edit needed.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: Retained 22.2: "Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly..."; the contradicting remote-access grant in original 22.1 is deleted.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: Revised 22.1 limits audits to once in any 12-month period, which satisfies the once-per-year fallback.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Revised 22.1 requires 30 days' written notice, exceeding the 15-day fallback minimum.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: Retained 22.2 places costs on Vendor unless underpayment exceeds five percent, which is within (and better than) the 10 percent fallback trigger.

reasons: Original 22.1 was walk-away (unlimited, unannounced audits with remote system access); the replacement inserts exactly the eight preferred parameters not already present and deletes only the remote-access and no-notice language, so the deviation finding is correct.
Cost allocation and the no-direct-access bar were already at or better than preferred in 22.2 and were correctly left untouched rather than duplicated in 22.1, avoiding duplicate operative terms.

Sections 22.2 and 22.3 (confidentiality of findings, copy of report, shortfall resolution, exclusions from audit scope) survive unchanged; no dangling cross-reference or undefined term is created, and the prior contradiction between 22.1's remote-access grant and 22.2's access bar is resolved in Customer's favour.
No extras were added — no survival tail, expense allocation, procedures, or requirements outside the AUDIT checklist.
